themes_detail.label: Water Quality Crisis This Week
themes_detail.summary: Water quality complaints spiked to 3 reports this week in East Flatbush, a 1,100% increase over the 0.2 weekly average from the prior 8 weeks, suggesting a potential contamination event or system failure affecting residents' drinking water.
evidence: 3 water quality complaints filed THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,100% spike, z-score: 6.35)
Concurrent spike in drinking complaints: 3 reports last week vs. 0.2 avg (same statistical signature)
No prior pattern in district; represents sudden emergence of new public health concern
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection to determine if water main break, contamination, or quality testing failure triggered complaints
Interview affected residents in the specific blocks where complaints clustered; obtain photos/samples if available

themes_detail.label: Graffiti Explosion Spreading
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints exploded to 26 reports two weeks ago, a 1,633% surge above the 1.5 weekly baseline, indicating either a coordinated tagging campaign or rapid community infrastructure deterioration in East Flatbush.
evidence: 26 graffiti complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 1.5 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (1,633% spike, z-score: 18.52, highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Spike occurred in discrete timeframe, suggesting localized event or organized activity rather than gradual deterioration
No sustained follow-up visible in current week data; suggests either resolution or reporting lag
reporting_angles: Map the 26 complaints geographically to identify whether graffiti is concentrated on specific blocks, buildings, or transit infrastructure
Contact NYPD and Parks Department to determine if crews have responded; ask about any known tagging crews or gang activity

themes_detail.label: Air Quality Deterioration Last Week
themes_detail.summary: Air quality complaints jumped to 6 reports last week, a 500% increase over the 1.0 weekly average, signaling potential industrial emissions, construction dust, or traffic-related pollution affecting East Flatbush residents.
evidence: 6 air quality complaints filed last week vs. 1.0 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (500% spike, z-score: 5.0)
Concurrent spike in smoking/vaping complaints (10 last week vs. 3.9 avg, +158%) suggests public health awareness or outdoor air contamination visibility
301 DOB building permits filed in district (168 alterations, 79 new buildings) — active construction may be source of dust/emissions
reporting_angles: Cross-reference air quality complaint locations with active construction sites from DOB permit data to assess correlation
Contact NYC Department of Environmental Protection regarding air quality monitoring; check if district near any industrial facilities or highways with increased traffic

themes_detail.label: Smoking/Vaping Complaints Surging
themes_detail.summary: Smoking and vaping complaints rose to 10 reports last week, a 158% increase over the 3.9 weekly average, reflecting either enforcement of smoking restrictions or heightened community concern about secondhand smoke in shared spaces.
evidence: 10 smoking/vaping complaints filed last week vs. 3.9 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (158% spike, z-score: 3.99)
Spike correlates temporally with air quality spike (both last week), suggesting possible shared cause or heightened environmental awareness
No prior district-wide initiative visible; pattern may reflect resident complaints about specific locations (bars, parks, housing buildings)
reporting_angles: Identify whether complaints are concentrated in multi-family housing, parks, transit, or commercial spaces to target investigation
Contact NYC Department of Health to ask if there's been recent enforcement action or public campaign about smoking compliance

themes_detail.label: Abandoned Bikes Piling Up
themes_detail.summary: Abandoned bike complaints spiked to 3 reports three weeks ago, a 2,300% surge over the 0.1 weekly baseline, indicating either a rapid accumulation of discarded bike-share or personal bikes clogging sidewalks and public space.
evidence: 3 abandoned bike complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.1 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (2,300% spike, z-score: 8.69)
Spike is dated; no current-week follow-up visible, suggesting either cleanup occurred or complaints shifted to different category
No known recent bike-share service change or expansion in East Flatbush visible in public data
reporting_angles: Contact NYC Department of Transportation and Citi Bike operator to determine if there were abandoned bikes from stolen/damaged docking stations
Investigate whether spike correlates with specific location (transit hub, schoolyard, park) to assess ongoing impact
